findings.reason: the node cannot implement the section as written, and the two shapes it could choose instead (wrapper enters the scopes for reads only and write tools own their own entry, or a new close helper that reaches into the private ContextVars) differ in which paths get one boundary, so the write paths, case 1 and case 7 all move with the choice.
findings.text: §2 says the scopes are entered inside the executor callable "around the tool body", and in the next sentence that "`edit_plan` closes both scopes before it writes, and any read after the write in the same call opens them afresh"; but the scope is a `@contextmanager` (`metadata_index.discovery_file_scope`, reckon/metadata_index.py:100-119; `resources.resource_scan_scope`, reckon/resources.py:507-538) whose token is held by whoever entered it, and the body holds no token, so it cannot exit a scope the wrapper opened — and a re-entry after the write would join the still-open region rather than open afresh, because the scope's documented rule is that "a nested entry joins the region already open" (metadata_index.py:105-107) and "nested scopes share the outermost one" (resources.py:518). `_edit_plan_tool` does read after the write today (`_review_owed_fields` and `_plan_readiness_fields`, reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:2247-2255), and `resource_scan_scope`'s own docstring says a resource created inside the scope "stays invisible until the scope exits" (resources.py:516-517), so the post-write read returns the pre-write covered observation and the seventh case ("a read after the write returns the written value") fails; the same contradiction makes case 1's "validates the covered tree once" unmeetable for `edit_plan`, since a close-and-reopen must validate a second time
